top_story: Pressure across the Israeli-Palestinian-Lebanese arena intensified as an eight-day settler and military siege in Qusra, following at least six days of home seizures and family expulsions, left Palestinian residents cut off from water and aid and underscored how coercive control is spreading through daily life in the West Bank. In Gaza, reconstruction remains constrained by wartime governance, where unstable ceasefire conditions, renewed bombardment, and external management of relief are shaping who can return, rebuild, and exercise authority. The sharpest escalation came on 15 August, when Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 11 people, including children, in the deadliest toll since the June truce and widened the sense that front-line restraints are eroding. Taken together, these developments point to a regional security order in which nominal ceasefires and reconstruction frameworks are no longer containing violence but are being used to structure it.
